rationale: This is a near-mechanical rediscovery of the archived "Debt Proceeds Liquidity Leak" (identical dltis-vs-cash-change base with the identical lct/act–NEG(oancf) conditioner), differing only in whether the two components are combined by subtraction or rank-product, so it cannot cleanly diagnose why that signal's fmb and alpha evidence diverged.

The interaction of new borrowing with a senior (preferred) payout claim is a genuinely distinct mechanism relative to the archive's separate preferred-payout and debt-issuance signals, though RANK of the mostly-zero dvt−dvc series will produce heavy ties and the effective sample may collapse to a small preferred-paying, debt-issuing subset.

The "payout capacity reallocated from common to senior claims" story is economically coherent and not literally in the archive, but it is a fairly direct multiplicative splice of two already-tested components (Preferred Payout Debt Overhang and Solvency Dividend Retrenchment) and the triple rank-product over two sparse payout variables risks a thin, unstable long-short leg.

The base term MIN(dltis, sstk) is taken verbatim from the archived "Dual-Issuance Working-Capital Stress" and the conditioner is taken verbatim from "Post-Equity Cash Burn Continuation," making this a recombination of previously tested parts rather than a new mechanism or a diagnosis of their weak Fama-MacBeth slopes.

Internally flawed construction: MIN of a strictly nonnegative level (dltis/at) and a signed first difference (NEG(DELTA(che/at))) is dominated by the cash-change term whenever cash rises, so the "prior debt issuance" leg is silently switched off for much of the sample and the signal largely degenerates to an equity-issuance × cash-decline variant of the archived "Debt-Then-Equity Rescue Spiral."

The equity-issuance-plus-debt-repayment base and the accrual (ib−oancf) conditioner are both already in the archive ("Dilutive Debt-Service Swap," "Equity-Issued Debt-Service Burden"), so swapping in NEG(DELTA(che)) is a cosmetic conditioner substitution on a family that has repeatedly delivered alpha without cross-sectional slope support.
